data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The resolution lies in an evolutionary epistemology where corroboration functions as a selection mechanism analogous to natural selection, bypassing the need for inductive justification.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the evolutionary analogy fails to explain why we expect the 'fittest' theory to work in novel domains (the problem of projectibility).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the selection pressure (testing) is not truly independent of the theory's content.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The mechanism is 'conjecture and refutation as evolution': theories compete for survival. Corroboration is not a measure of probability but a record of survival in a hostile environment of testing. We prefer the survivor not because we induce it will survive tomorrow, but because it is the only one currently adapted to the known constraints. The 'preference' is simply the state of having eliminated the competitors. The cost is accepting that science does not progress toward truth in a linear, probable sense, but merely eliminates error, leaving us with the 'fittest' falsehoods.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
